SMTO-GWT-0053 — SMTO has no network path to the Gateway computer

GUID: 3ef15304-bd4e-4aae-a536-b9e14885ca5d
Slug: gateway-no-route
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • The computer running SMTO can't reach the Gateway computer's network at all right now, so no connection was made and this request was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the Gateway computer is switched on, awake and connected to its network. A computer that is off or offline can't be reached by any route.
  2. If the Gateway is on a work or private network, make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to it too, for example that its VPN is on. Without that connection, the SMTO computer has no way through to the Gateway's network.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit, check that Host is the Gateway's correct address, then select Check connection. An old or mistyped address can point to a network the SMTO computer can't reach.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows the Gateway as connected, and your request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your network, along with the Gateway's address. Don't switch the Task to a different Gateway just to get past this unless you really meant the work to run there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Connecting to the selected inbound Gateway failed with EHOSTUNREACH or ENETUNREACH before the request was sent; the Server host has no usable network route to that address.

What this means

  • Connection setup returned EHOSTUNREACH or ENETUNREACH before request transmission, establishing an unreachable host or network at that boundary. This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.

Why this can happen

  • Connection setup returned EHOSTUNREACH or ENETUNREACH before request transmission, establishing an unreachable host or network at that boundary.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the controller's route to the selected endpoint and any required VPN or network boundary; do not assume a particular firewall rule caused it.

How to fix it

  • From the Server host, check the route to the Gateway address (ip route get, ping or traceroute), VPN status, and firewall rules that answer with host- or network-unreachable. Restore the intended route or firewall access rather than pointing the work at a different Gateway, then use Check connection.
  • Restore the intended network/VPN route or authorized firewall access.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended network path becomes reachable and the selected Gateway identity verifies.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
